PARTMENT OF PARKS AND RECREATION

(916) 445-8006
March'6, 1978
Mr. James L. Goggin
David J. Powers and Associates
1530 The Alameda, Suite 200
San Jose, CA 95126
Dear Mr. Goggin:
I have received your letter of January 27, 1978, regarding the San Jose Community Development Block Grant Program, Santa Clara County.
No California State Historical Landmarks, State Points of Historical Interest, or sites on the National Register of Historic Places are currently listed in the project area. However, Santa Clara County Archeological Site #230 is located in the vicinity of the Olinder neighborhood. The Alviso National Register Historic District is adjacent to the Alviso Project Area.
Projects assisted by federal funding or licensed by federal permits must comply with the National Historic Preservation Act of 1966. Properties possessing historical, archeological, architectural, or cultural values within the project's area of potential environmental impact must be identified for possible inclusion in the National Register of Historic Places. The twenty residential structures scheduled for demolition must be assessed for their architectural, historical, or engineering significance.
The Office of Historic Preservation would appreciate an opportunity to review and comment on the EIR'S prepared for the San Jose Block Grant Program. I am also enclosing a copy of a Memorandum of Understanding, developed by the Office of Historic Preservation, to assist in the County of San Diego's Community Development Block Grant Program. Please contact Eugene Itogawa of my staff at (916) 322-8701 to discuss the Memorandum of Understanding.
Sincerely yours,
Knowernailin
Dr. Knox Mellon State Historic Preservation Officer
